subject: health
title: Explicit model: modifiable and non-modifiable factors, stated without moralizing
focus: modifiable and non-modifiable factors, stated without moralizing
essentialQuestion: How do decisions made now compound over decades, without turning that into fear or blame?
keyPoints: Modifiable factors can sometimes change, while non-modifiable factors cannot; neither category justifies blame because access, constraints, and biology also shape outcomes.
Represent long-term health as an interaction among biology, environment, access, behavior, and support; distinguish changeable from fixed factors without assigning blame.

For modifiable and non-modifiable factors, stated without moralizing, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Build a twenty-year wellbeing model for a fictional adult, showing which inputs are inside personal control, which are structural, and which supports change the picture most.
studentTask: Build a causal web for a supplied fictional case about modifiable and non-modifiable factors, stated without moralizing. Include biological, environmental or access, behavioral, and support factors; mark which factors can change, add one realistic support, and explain why the web does not assign blame.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in modifiable and non-modifiable factors, stated without moralizing; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the modifiable and non-modifiable factors, stated without moralizing task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: The model may be drawn, tabled, narrated, or assembled from supplied factor cards.
extensionChallenge: Apply modifiable and non-modifiable factors, stated without moralizing under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of modifiable and non-modifiable factors, stated without moralizing in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.
